Last month, after the television tracking app TV Time ceased operations, one of its co-founders, Antonio Pinto, immediately announced the launch of a brand-new film and television tracking app called Bingers, which focuses on richer social features. Details are as follows.

Bingers is now available for download

Whip Media previously announced that it would shut down the television tracking app TV Time, and one of the app's co-founders immediately announced the launch of Bingers, positioning it as a "watchlist with speed, aesthetics, and fun community features."

According to TechCrunch, Bingers is now available for download on iOS and Android platforms. For users still searching for a TV Time alternative, this app can be seen as the "spiritual successor" to the now-defunct platform—TV Time was once one of the most widely used television tracking apps in the world.

Former TV Time users who have backed up their data through the export tool can import their database into Bingers, seamlessly continuing their existing viewing records; users who never exported their data, or new users who have never used a television tracking app before, can start building their watchlist from scratch.

Bingers places great emphasis on community-driven features, including personal profiles, commenting on show ratings, GIF stickers, polls, and character popularity votes, among others. Pinto told TechCrunch that these are precisely the features that made TV Time so popular over the years:

If users simply want to track the TV shows and movies they have watched, Bingers offers dedicated watchlist and viewing history features. Similar to TV Time, the platform also displays a calendar of upcoming and premiere episodes, along with a countdown function showing how many days remain until broadcast.

Bingers is available for free download on the App Store and currently has no in-app purchases.
